scope: Visual additions to /app only: original Good Legs coach in the hero and original strength/recovery artwork in the two existing feature sections. No marketing paragraphs, offers or product claims changed.

sections.readerQuestion: Is Good Legs recognisably the same Roadman product as the one on getgoodlegs.com?
sections.usefulAnswer: The original brown-and-white cat, branded clothing and Good Legs wordmark establish the shared product identity beside the existing description and waitlist link.
sections.evidence: Unmodified coach-hero.webp from the current getgoodlegs.com homepage; source URL and SHA-256 are in docs/good-legs-visual-sources.json.
sections.editorialDecision: Use the complete original character at its natural aspect ratio. Desktop rendering shows both ears, tail and shoes intact, with no overlap over the text or button.

sections.readerQuestion: Which part of the product concerns strength training?
sections.usefulAnswer: The original barbell-squat illustration makes the strength section immediately identifiable beside the existing explanation of previous lifts and session logging.
sections.evidence: Unmodified scene-strength-1536.webp from getgoodlegs.com; dimensions 1536 by 1031. It is mascot artwork, not a new exercise prescription or app screenshot.
sections.editorialDecision: Place the artwork immediately above its related heading, preserve the full barbell and feet, and use a light background for legibility.

sections.readerQuestion: Which part of the product concerns recovery?
sections.usefulAnswer: The original resting/headphones illustration identifies the recovery section and gives it the same visual weight as strength.
sections.evidence: Unmodified scene-recovery-1536.webp from getgoodlegs.com; dimensions 1536 by 1000. The alt text identifies the cat mascot resting.
sections.editorialDecision: Match the strength image container proportions, contain the entire illustration and keep the existing recovery explanation beside it.

claimsAndSources: No new scientific, performance or product capability claims. Image provenance is recorded with original URLs and byte hashes. No new person, partner endorsement or product result is invented.
examplesAndReasoning: No training example added. The rejected Thursday/example-week table remains absent. The illustrations identify the brand and its two existing product areas; they do not supply training doses.
voiceAndCuts: The existing marketing paragraphs and headings are unchanged. Added alt text describes the original artwork plainly. No slogans, invented testimonials, interface labels or internal product boundaries were added.
desktopReview: Reviewed the signed-in Vercel preview at 1363 by 936 CSS pixels on 7 September 2026, commit f9a0b083effb7b10d4aaa010552aa9d44518de41. All three images loaded. Hero box was 331.28 by 660 pixels; feature image boxes were 464 by 288 pixels. Document width was 1355, with no horizontal overflow. Hero and feature-section screenshots showed uncropped artwork, readable text and visible CTA. Existing cookie banner was dismissed through its Reject Non-Essential control for the feature review.
mobileReview: Not yet verified in a rendered mobile viewport. Source inspection confirms a single-column layout below the desktop breakpoint, a 320-pixel contained hero image and contained feature images with reserved aspect ratios. The available browser has no viewport-resizing capability; keyboard attempts did not change its viewport. A phone screenshot or editor mobile review is still required before this review is complete.
productAndOfferAccuracy: Existing prelaunch iPhone status and Not Done Yet access at launch remain unchanged. Both Good Legs outbound URLs retain their original attribution parameters. The artwork is reused from the user-owned Good Legs site; no stock UI or redesigned mascot was introduced.
